        ### Question
        A 44-year-old man with HIV comes to the physician for a routine follow-up examination. He has been noncompliant with his antiretroviral medication regimen for several years. He appears chronically ill and fatigued. CD4+ T-lymphocyte count is 405/mm3 (N ≥ 500). Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?

        ### Options
        opa. Violaceous lesions on skin exam
opb. Cotton-wool spots on fundoscopy
opc. Multifocal demyelination on brain MRI
opd. Ring-enhancing lesions on brain MRI
ope. Ground-glass opacities on chest CT

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: Noncompliance with antiretroviral medication -> decreased CD4+ T-lymphocyte count -> 80% CHAIN: Decreased CD4+ T-lymphocyte count -> increased risk of opportunistic infections -> 90% CHAIN: Increased risk of opportunistic infections -> possible multifocal demyelination on brain MRI -> 70% CHAIN: Possible multifocal demyelination on brain MRI -> ring-enhancing lesions on brain MRI -> 60% CHAIN: Ring-enhancing lesions on brain MRI -> 40% CHAIN: Noncompliance with antiretroviral medication -> chronic illness and fatigue -> 70% CHAIN: Chronic illness and fatigue -> possible ground-glass opacities on chest CT -> 80%
